question: Should OpenClaw adopt these four named opt-in hosting profiles as its initial supported deployment catalog after the readiness RFC is accepted?
rationale: The RFC adds a persistent product/configuration and support contract, including reverse-proxy trust semantics and release-gate ownership; correctness of the prose cannot determine whether those are the intended public commitments.

options.title: Approve the bounded V1 catalog
options.body: Accept the four opt-in profiles, subject to owner-reviewed reverse-proxy security criteria and a defined packaged release-proof lane.

options.title: Accept readiness only
options.body: Land or decide the reusable readiness contract first while deferring named profile selection and conformance claims.

options.title: Narrow the catalog
options.body: Retain only the postures with clear support ownership and defer proxy or node-mode profiles until their owners approve the predicates.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded V1 catalog
recommendation.body: Accept the four opt-in profiles, subject to owner-reviewed reverse-proxy security criteria and a defined packaged release-proof lane.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the connected readiness and hosting-profile RFCs and can clarify the intended proposal boundary, while final product acceptance remains with repository leadership.
